Hijo de Hetum I e Isabel, sufrió cautive: Son of Hetum I and Elizabeth, he was held captive after the Mamluk invasion of 1266. As king he continued to seek Mongolian support against Egypt. His numerous offspring linked Armenia with Byzantium and the Lusignan.

Rey de la Armenia cilicia por su matrimo: King of the Armenian cilitia for his marriage to Elizabeth, sought in the Mongols an ally against his regional enemies. That bet also conditioned Antioch's policy, united with his family for the marriage of his daughter Sibylla.

Esposa de León II y madre de una amplia: Wife of Leo II and mother of a large royal offspring, she appears with her family in a famous image of Armenian manuscript. Her children occupied the crown or established links with Byzantium and Cyprus, giving this generation a great Mediterranean projection.
Consorte de la dinastía Hetúmida. Su tra: Consort of the Hethumid dynasty. Their life is linked to Cilician Armenia, Byzantium.
Alternó la corona con retiros religiosos: He alternated the crown with religious retreats and shared power with members of his family. He sought the Mongol alliance in front of the Mamluks, but he died killed by a Mongol chief along with his nephew Leon. His restorations are recorded separately.
Recibió el trono después de la retirada: He received the throne after the withdrawal of his brother Hetum and later shared it with him. The dispute between brothers ended with his deposition and death in captivity. His son Leon regained the rights of his line.
Aprovechó la ausencia de sus hermanos pa: He took advantage of the absence of his brothers to take the crown. Inner struggles weakened the position of the kingdom vis-à-vis its neighbours and ended with its deposition. His brief government is part of the successor crisis of the sons of Leo II.
Desplazó a su hermano Smbat y ocupó brev: He displaced his brother Smbat and briefly occupied the crown before returning power to Hetum II. His reign was another phase of a dynastic dispute involving several sons of Leo II.
Hermano de Hetum II, obtuvo la corona tr: Brother of Hetum II, he obtained the crown after the murders of 1307. He tried to sustain the kingdom between the Mamluk threat and the search for Western support. Discussions on religious union accompanied his foreign policy.

Hija de León II y Keran, se casó con Ama: Daughter of Leo II and Keran, she married Amalric of Lusignan. After the death of her husband, her family was caught up in the struggles of the Armenian court. Her descendants inherited the claim that led the Lusignans to the Cilician throne.
Hija de Hetum I y esposa de Bohemundo VI: Daughter of Hetum I and wife of Bohemundo VI. Her marriage reinforced the alliance between Armenia, Antioch and Tripoli; after the death of her husband she intervened in county politics during the Bohemundo VII minority.
Gran señor armenio y padre de Hetum I, d: Grand Armenian lord and father of Hetum I, played a central role in the crisis that led his son to the throne. His family’s marriage policy united Elizabeth’s continuity with the predominance of the Hetumids.
Hijo de Teodoro III, accedió al trono ba: Son of Theodore III, he acceded to the throne under the tutelage of his uncle Hetum II. Both were killed by the Mongol chief Bilarghu. The crisis showed that the alliance with the Mongols did not guarantee the security of the Armenian monarchy.
Heredó la corona siendo niño, bajo una r: He inherited the crown as a child, under a regency that accumulated great power. His search for Latino help and fighting with nobility aggravated instability. He died without an heir who maintained the male line of the Hetumidas.
Fue elegido tras el asesinato de Constan: He was elected after the assassination of Constantine II in a kingdom threatened by the Mamluks. His government sought to sustain the remaining squares through military and diplomatic agreements. It belonged to a hetumatized collateral branch.
Gobernó durante la contracción final del: He ruled during the final contraction of the kingdom and tried to find support in the face of Mamluk pressure. Internal divisions persisted and ended his murder. The crown then passed to Leon de Lusignan.

Nacido Guido de Lusignan, aceptó la coro: Born Guido de Lusignan, he accepted the crown after the death of his cousin Leo IV. His project of approach to the Latin Church found resistance among the nobles. He was murdered, putting an end to the first Lusignan reign in Cilicia.
Se casó con Sibila de Armenia y particip: He married Sibyla of Armenia and participated in the approach of Christian powers to the Mongols. The Mamluk conquest of Antioch in 1268 left him ruling Tripoli and retaining only the title of the lost principality.

Hijo de Amalarico e Isabel, administró A: Son of Amalric and Elizabeth, he administered Armenia during the transition to the Lusignan monarchy and favored the candidacy of his brother Guido. His son Leon would be the last king to effectively rule the Cilician kingdom.
Margarita de Lusignan, reina de Armenia: Margaret of Lusignan, Queen of Armenia
Hija de Hugo III de Chipre y esposa de T: The daughter of Hugo III of Cyprus and wife of Theodore III of Armenia, she was the mother of Leo III. Her marriage is one of the direct links between the two monarchies, prior to the Lusignans' access to the Cilician crown.

Hijo del emperador Fernando I, archiduqu: Son of Emperor Fernando I, archduke of Inner Austria since 1564. His son Fernando II took this branch of Styria to the imperial throne.

Recibió Pfalz-Neuburg de Otón Enrique en: He received pfalzo-Neuburg from Otto Henry in 1557. His son Philip Louis after his death in 1569, and his sequence belonged to the principality of Neuburg, and his father's opposition to his opposition.
Hermano de Carlos V y fundador de la ram: Brother of Charles V and founder of the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs. He reunited Austria, Bohemia and much of Hungary and succeeded his brother in imperial dignity.
Emperador del Sacro Imperio y soberano d: Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche Condado, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Güeldres in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

Emperador Habsburgo de perfil relativame: Emperor Habsburg of relatively conciliatory profile in a Europe divided by the Reformation. He also ruled Bohemia and Hungary within the complex Central European monarchy of his home.
Reina de Castilla y Aragón, hija de los: Queen of Castile and Aragon, daughter of the Catholic Monarchs and mother of Charles V. She retained her crowns while Philip, Ferdinand and Charles successively exercised the government.

Cuarto hijo de Enrique II y Leonor de Aq: Fourth son of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, he ruled Brittany since his marriage to Duchess Constance in 1181. He participated in the rebellions against his father and died in Paris in 1186; his posthumous son Arthur inherited his rights.
Coronado en vida de su padre en 1170, nu: Crowned during his father’s lifetime in 1170, he never ruled in his own right, so the title is not recorded as a reign. He rebelled in 1173 and died before Henry II.

Tercer hijo de Enrique II y Leonor de Aq: Third son of Henry II and Leonor of Aquitaine, he was Duke of Aquitaine from 1172 and king of England from 1189 to 1199. He led the third crusade with Philip Augustus, defeated Saladin in Arsuf (1191) and negotiated the access of pilgrims to Jerusalem. Captured on his return by Leopold V of Austria, he passed into the hands of Emperor Henry VI until paying a huge ransom in 1194. He dedicated his last years to defending Normandy in front of France and died in the siege of Châlus.
Esposa de Guillermo II de Sicilia (1177): Wife of William II of Sicily (1177) and after sending and accompanying his brother Ricardo at his crusade Raimundo VI of Tolosa (1196).
Hija de Enrique II y Leonor de Aquitania: The daughter of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine, married William II of Sicily in 1177. Widow, accompanied his brother Ricardo at his third crusade and married Raimundo VI of Tolosa in 1196. He died in 1199 and was buried at Fontevraud.
Reina consorte de Sicilia · Condesa cons: Queen consort of Sicily · Countess consort of Toulouse
Consorte de la dinastía Plantagenet. Su: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile, England.
Rey de Inglaterra cuyo reinado estuvo ma: King of England whose reign was marked by the loss of much of the Plantagenet continental domains and by the crisis that led to the Magna Carta of 1215.
Hija de Enrique I de Inglaterra y viuda: Daughter of Henry I of England and widow of Emperor Henry V, she contested the throne with Stephen of Blois from 1135 to 1153. In 1141 she styled herself ‘Lady of the English’, but was never crowned. The Atlas therefore does not record that title as an effective reign.
Hija de Enrique I de Inglaterra, se casó: Daughter of Henry I of England, she married Emperor Henry V and, after being widowed, Geoffrey of Anjou. Named heir by her father, she fought Stephen of Blois in the English civil war known as the Anarchy without ever being crowned, and secured the succession of her son Henry II in 1154.
Casada con Ricardo I en Limassol (Chipre: Married with Ricardo I at Cleansol (Cyprus) at 1191, during the third crusade. He's the only queen of England who's never been on his way to his kingdom.
Hija de Sancho VI de Navarra, se casó co: Daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre, she married Ricardo I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, during the crusade. She never lived in England; after widowing she lived in Le Mans, which was part of her dowry, and there she founded the Abbey of L’Épau, where she is buried.
Guerrero y servidor de varios reyes Plan: He was also a man of Irish lands and a servant of several Plantagenet kings for his marriage to Elizabeth de Clare. At the end of his life his government was directed during Henry's minority III, linking Leinster's policy with the survival of the British monarchy.
Hija de Petru Rareș y Elena Branković, s: The daughter of Petru Rareș and Elena Branković, she married Alejandro Lăpușneanu. She intervened in the continuity of her family and, after the removal and death of her husband, exercised the regency of Bogdan IV. Her ancestry links the Moldovan sovereigns with the family of the Serbian despots.
Príncipe de Moldavia e hijo de Esteban e: Prince of Moldova and son of Stephen the Great. He tried to maintain an active policy between Poland, Hungary and the Ottoman Empire during a time when Moldovan autonomy was increasingly difficult to sustain.
Hija de Jovan Branković y esposa de Petr: Daughter of Jovan Branković and wife of Petru Rareș, brought to Moldova the connection with the Serbian despots. He intervened in the government during the minority of his son Esteban. His daughter Ruxandra also became a consort and regent Moldava. Chiajna, daughter of another union of Petru, was his stepdaughter.
Gobernó Moldavia en dos etapas, separada: He ruled Moldova in two phases, separated by a deposition. His marriage with Roxandra Rareș tightened his links with Petru Rareș's offspring.
Hijo de Alejandro Lăpușneanu y Ruxandra: The son of Alexander Lăpușneanu and Ruxandra Rareș, he joined the government during his minority. His mother exercised regency until 1570.

Hija de Petru Rareș y de su primera espo: Daughter of Petru Rareș and his first wife Maria, she married Mircea Ciobanul. After her husband’s death she directed the government of her son Petru. His deposition in 1568 drove the family into exile. She is still recorded in 1587, but the precise year of her death is unknown.
Voivoda de Moldavia, 1504–1517. Príncipe: Voivode of Moldova, 1504–1517. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.
Príncipe de Moldavia durante casi medio: Prince of Moldova for about half a century and one of the central figures of Eastern XV's. He defended his principality with respect to Ottoman, Polish and Hungarian and was associated with an intense military and religious policy.
Voivoda de Moldavia, 1449–1451. Príncipe: Voivode of Moldova, 1449–1451. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.
Príncipe de Moldavia recordado por un la: Prince of Moldova, remembered for a long period of political stability. He strengthened the institutions of the principality and maneuvered between Poland, Hungary and its Black Sea neighbours.
Voivoda de Moldavia, 1391–1394. Príncipe: Voivode of Moldova, 1391–1394. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.
Se alió con los Habsburgo contra los oto: He allied himself with the Habsburgs against the Ottomans and defeated Andrés Bathory in 1599. For a few months he ruled Wallachia, Transylvania and Moldova, with different positions and legitimacys. Personal union was brief and did not create a modern national state.
Reina de Suecia, hija de Gustavo II Adol: Queen of Sweden and daughter of Gustavus Adolphus, she was renowned for her intellectual and cultural interests. She abdicated in 1654, converted to Catholicism and spent much of her life in Rome.
Olomouc ocupada por el ejército sueco; n: Oromouc occupied by the Swedish army and not sovereignty over all Moravia

Christina is the Swedish sovereign during this period; military command and administration belong to her officers. She receives no margravial title and is not assigned all Moravia.
Hija de Gustavo II Adolfo y de María Leo: Daughter of Gustavo II Adolfo and Maria Leonor of Brandenburg, born in Stockholm in 1626 and inherited the throne in 1632. She was educated as an heir prince and ruled a regency presided over by Chancellor Oxenstierna until her majority in 1644.
Westfalia y la corte de Estocolmo: Westphalia and the Court of Stockholm
Impulsó la paz de Westfalia (1648), que: He promoted the peace of Westphalia (1648), which gave Sweden Western Pomerania, Bremen and Verden. He brought wise men and artists, including René Descartes, to Stockholm, who died there in 1650. He refused to marry and managed to get the Riksdag to recognize his cousin Carlos Gustavo as heir.
En 1654 abdicó en él y se convirtió en s: In 1654 he abdicated in it and became secret to Catholicism, making it public in Innsbruck in 1655. He settled in Rome, where he protected musicians such as Corelli and Alessandro Scarlatti and gathered notable collections. He unsuccessfully tried to obtain the crown of Naples and that of Poland. He died in Rome in 1689 and is buried in St. Peter.

Rey de Polonia desde 1648, hermano de La: King of Poland since 1648, brother of Ladislaus IV. His reign suffered the Cossack rebellion of Jmelnitski and the Swedish invasion known as the Flood; abdicated in 1668.

Hija de Carlos IX y María del Palatinado: Daughter of Charles IX and Mary of the Palatinate. Her son Carlos X Gustavo succeeded Cristina of Sweden: the dynastic name change did not break the family continuity by female line.
Rey de Polonia y durante un tiempo tambi: King of Poland and for a time also of Sweden. His double inheritance Vasa and Jagelón fed long wars for the Baltic and dynastic conflicts between the two crowns.
Hijo de Gustavo Vasa y Margarita Leijonh: Son of Gustav Vasa and Margaret Leijonhufvud. As duke and leader of the opposition to his nephew Sigismund, he drove the change of power that excluded the Polish branch from the Swedish throne. He was the father of Gustavus Adolphus and of Catherine, whose descendants included Charles X Gustav.
Depuso a su hermano Erico XIV y buscó un: He deposed his brother Eric XIV and sought a middle course in religious policy. His marriage to Catherine Jagiellon linked the Vasas to the Polish succession.
Leopoldo I del Sacro Imperio: Leopold I of the Holy Roman Empire
Emperador Habsburgo durante casi medio s: Emperor Habsburg for almost half a century. His reign was marked by wars against Louis XIV and by the great confrontation with the Ottoman Empire culminated in Vienna in 1683.
José I del Sacro Imperio: Joseph I of the Holy Roman Empire
Emperador Habsburgo durante la Guerra de: Emperor Habsburg during the Spanish War of Succession. He continued the policy of his father Leopold I and supported the candidacy of his brother Charles to the Spanish throne.
Carlos VI del Sacro Imperio: Charles VI of the Holy Roman Empire
Emperador Habsburgo y rival de Felipe V: Emperor Habsburg and rival of Philip V in the War of Succession. His house ruled Milan, Naples and Sardinia on different dates; he traded Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance to Mary Theresa.
Elector del Palatinado y, durante el inv: The elector of the Palatinate and, during the winter of 1619–1620, king of Bohemia. His acceptance of the Bohemian crown turned a constitutional crisis into one of the triggers of the Thirty Years' War.
Heredó un ducado ocupado en gran parte p: He inherited a duchy occupied largely by other powers. His service to Charles V and Philip II, and especially the victory of San Quintin, contributed to the territorial recovery agreed at Cateau-Cambresis.

His service to Charles V and Philip II, and especially the victory of Saint Quintin, contributed to the territorial recovery agreed upon in Cateau-Cambrésis. Consort of the Valois-Angulema dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Savoy.

Noble de la dinastía Saboya. Su trayecto: Noble of the Savoy dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Savoy.

Hijo de Carlos I y Blanca de Monferrato,: The son of Charles I and Blanca de Montferrat, Savoy inherited before his first birthday. His mother exercised the regency.

Heredó el ducado de su hermano Filiberto: He inherited the duchy of his brother Filiberto I. His marriage to Blanca de Montferrat reinforced Savoy's expectations of the Palaeologists' heritage, while the intervention in Saluzzo confronted him with French interests.
Consorte de la dinastía Saboya. Su traye: Consort of the Savoy dynasty. Their life is linked to Milan.

Among his sons were Victor Amadeus I and Thomas Francis, for whom he continued the branch of Carignano.

Heredó los derechos de su hermano Mateo: He inherited the rights of his brother Matthew and was the figure who sustained Foix's patrimonial continuity by passing to the descendants of the Grailly. Her husband Archambaud participated in the government for that marriage. The distinction between the heiress and the consort allows to read correctly the origin of the Foix-Grailly line.
Continuó la rama de Castellbó y fue padr: He continued the branch of Castellbó and was the father of Matthew and Elizabeth. Neither of the two inherited Fébus Gaston's Foix by direct descent: the link came from a collateral line. Its incorporation into the tree allows to follow that relationship without making the successor the son of the former ruler.
Su matrimonio con Isabel de Foix-Castell: His marriage with Elizabeth of Faix- Castellbó linked him to his open succession after Mateo's death. He participated in his wife's inheritance and was father of John I of Faix. The descendants retained his name Faix but his male descent came from Grailly.
Hijo de Isabel de Foix-Castellbó y Archa: The son of Isabella de Foix-Castellbó and Archambaud of Grailly, he continued the heritage of Foix under a new male descent. His marriage to Juana de Albret connected both houses before the navarra royal union of the end of the 15th century. His son Gastón IV married Leonor of Navarre.
Miembro de la rama de Castellbó, sucedió: A member of the Castellbó branch, he succeeded Gaston Fébus in Foix and Béarn in 1391. His rule was brief and ended without descendants to continue his line. The inheritance passed to his sister Isabella, wife of Archambaud de Grailly, opening a new dynastic phase.
Gastón de Foix, hijo de Fébus: Gaston of Foix, son of Fébus
Hijo de Gastón Fébus e Inés de Navarra,: Son of Gaston Fébus and Inés de Navarra, he was called to continue the line of the condom. He died in 1380, before his father, in the context of a violent family conflict. His absence in the succession explains that, after the death of Fébus, he would inherit a side branch of the Foix.
La muerte de su hijo Gastón precedió a l: The death of his son Gaston preceded his count's. The continuity passed through a collateral branch, and did not pass through a offspring of his successor Mateo.
Conde de Foix y vizconde de Bearne, cono: Count of Foix and Viscount of Bearne, known as Gastón Fébus, ruled a heritage of great importance in the Pyrenees. His marriage to Inés de Navarra connected him to the Évreux.
Su matrimonio con Leonor de Navarra vinc: His marriage with Leonor de Navarra linked his house to his Navarre succession. He combined his prenaic interests with his service to his French monarchy.
Gastón de Foix, príncipe de Viana: Gaston of Foix, Prince of Viana
Hijo de Gastón IV de Foix y Leonor de Na: The son of Gaston IV of Foix and Leonor of Navarre, he married Magdalena of France. He was the father of Francisco Febo and Catherine. He died before his mother came to the Navarren throne, so the succession passed to the generation of his children without him becoming king.
Heredó Foix y Bearne siendo niño y fue p: He inherited Foix and Bearne as a child and was the father of Gastón Fébus. Hijo mayor de Felipe V, reinó apenas uno: Philip V's eldest son, he reigned only a few months in 1724 after his father's abdication. He died of smallpox at the age of seventeen and Philip V returned to the throne.
Consorte de la dinastía Borbón. Su traye: Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their life was connected with France, England.
Rey de España entre 1746 y 1759, hijo de: King of Spain between 1746 and 1759, son of Philip V and Maria Luisa of Savoy. He maintained a policy of neutrality and reforms with ministers such as Ensenada and Carvajal; he died without offspring.
Consorte de la dinastía Borbón. Su traye: Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their life was connected with France, Spain.
Hija de Enrique IV de Francia y María de: The daughter of Henry IV of France and Mary of Medici, she married Victor Amadeus I of Savoy. After widowing she defended the government of her children against the princes of the ducal family, including Thomas Francis of Carignano.
Rey de Francia durante gran parte del si: King of France during much of the eighteenth century. His reign combined courtly prestige, costly wars and growing fiscal and political problems inherited by his successors.

Consorte de la dinastía Ivrea-Borgoña. S: Consort of the Ivrea-Borgoña dynasty. Their life is linked to Aragon, Castile.
Hijo de Federico II, elegido rey de roma: Son of Frederick II, elected king of Romans in 1220 and ruler in Germany on behalf of his father. He rebelled against him in 1234, was deposed and died in prison in 1242.
Hijo de Emerico, coronado rey de Hungría: Son of Emerico, crowned king of Hungary as a child in 1204. His uncle Andrés took over the government; the little king died in Austrian exile in 1205.
Rey de Aragón y conde de Barcelona estre: King of Aragon and Count of Barcelona closely involved in the Occitan politics. He died in the battle of Muret in 1213, a decisive episode for the French expansion north of the Pyrenees.
Conde de Provenza, 1209–1245. Conde de l: Count of Provence, 1209–1245. Count of the Barcelona dynasty.
Hijo de Alfonso II de Aragón, gobernó Pr: The son of Alfonso II of Aragon, he ruled Provence in the name of his father since 1185 and was counted to his death in 1196. In 1193 he married Garría de Sabran, a heiress of Forcalquier, a county that thus joined Provence. He died in 1209; his son Ramón Berenguer succeeded him.
Rey de Aragón y gran protagonista de la: King of Aragon and great protagonist of the expansion of the Crown of Aragon. He conquered Mallorca and Valencia and left a decisive territorial and dynastic heritage for the Western Mediterranean.

Luis II de Hungría y Bohemia: Louis II of Hungary and Bohemia
Murió en la derrota de Mohács frente a S: He died in the defeat of Mohács in front of Soliman the Magnificent. His death opened the competition between Ferdinand of Habsburg and John of Zápolya for the Hungarian crown.

Hija de Felipe el Hermoso y Juana de Cas: The daughter of Philip the Beautiful and Joan of Castile, she married Cristian II of Denmark. Her marriage connected the Kalmar crisis with the Habsburg network. After Cristian’s deposition she accompanied the family into exile in the Netherlands, where she died.
Rodolfo II del Sacro Imperio: Rodolfo II of the Holy Roman Empire
Emperador Habsburgo que trasladó su cort: Emperor Habsburg who moved his court to Prague and brought together artists, astronomers and scholars. His political and religious difficulties weakened his authority over other members of the dynasty.
Matías I del Sacro Imperio: Mates I of the Holy Roman Empire
Emperador Habsburgo que arrebató progres: Emperor Habsburg who progressively seized power from his brother Rodolfo II. His reign prepared the successor and religious crisis that would lead to the Thirty Years' War.
Vladislao II de Bohemia y Hungría: Vladislaus II of Bohemia and Hungary
Unió las coronas de Bohemia y Hungría ba: He united the crowns of Bohemia and Hungary under the Jagellon house. The growing noble influence limited his ability to act in both kingdoms.
Su minoría mantuvo abierta la rivalidad: His minority prolonged the rivalry between the Zápolyas and Habsburgs. The agreement of Speyer in 1570 exchanged his claim to the Hungarian kingship for the title of Prince of Transylvania and the Parts of Hungary, giving shape to the new principality.
Procedente de Mukhrani, fue adoptado com: From Mukhrani, he was adopted as heir by Rostom and recognized by the Sah. He extended the influence of his family towards Kakheti and Imereti through his children. His trajectory combines Bagrationi legitimacy with the safavid investiture.
Príncipe de Mukhrani y padre de Vajtang: Prince of Mukhrani and father of Vajtang V. He participated in the Georgian resistance to the Safavids and died in Marabda. His son then reached the crown by means of a policy of understanding with Persia.
Alternó el trono de Kartli con el servic: He alternated the Kartli throne with military service to the shah. After losing the crown and recovering it nominally, he led Safavid forces in Afghanistan, where he died in a rebellion. Periods away from the kingdom have separate entries from his government in person.
Son of Vajtang V and father of Vajtang VI. He was responsible for the Georgian government and the safe court. His children were candidates for the throne at a time when the Persian investiture and local control did not always match.
Hijo de Vajtang V, fue instalado en dife: Vakhtang V’s son was installed at different times in Kakheti and Imereti. Repeated losses of the throne led him to exile in Russia, where he developed his literary activity. His career links the three territorial branches, each with its own crown.
Hija de Teimuraz I, fue reina consorte d: The daughter of Teimuraz I was Queen consort of Immericia and a decisive figure in his subsequent disputes. Following Alexander III's death, he acted against Bagat V and promoted Vajtang Tchutchunashvili. He died during another Western court crisis.
Buscó fortalecer la corona frente a los: He sought to strengthen the crown in front of the Dadiani and took advantage of Mingelia's successive changes to expand its influence. His marriage to Darejan, daughter of Teimuraz I, linked Imereti to the Kakheti branch.
Fue depuesto, cegado y restaurado repeti: He was repeatedly deposed, blinded and restored. His periods of rule reveal a monarchy shaped by noble factions, marriages and intervention by neighbouring principalities. Each restoration has a separate entry to preserve the chronology of the disputes.
Hijo de Teimuraz I y Jorashan, combatió: Son of Teimuraz I and Jorashan, he fought against Rostom and died at the Battle of Magharo. His son Heraclius continued the Kakhetian royal line, from which Teimuraz II and Heraclius II descended.
Hijo de Bagrat V, regresó al trono con a: Son of Bagrat V, returned to the throne with Ottoman support and faced the factions that favoured Archil. His two reigns ended in new expulsions; his death did not end the rivalry between the two lines.
Hija de Jorge X de Kartli y esposa de Te: Daughter of George X of Kartli and wife of Teimuraz I of Kakheti. The marriage strengthened cooperation between the two branches during their wars against Persia. Her children linked this generation to the later kings of Kakheti and Immericia.
Poeta y rey, alternó resistencia, negoci: A poet and king, he alternated resistance, negotiation and exile under pressure from Abbas I and his successors. The rebellion of 1625 allowed him to return and extend his authority to Kartli, but Rostom eventually displaced him. His family endured captivity, executions and displacement.
Pasó parte de su juventud en Rusia y aca: He spent part of his youth in Russia and eventually accepted Safavid investiture. He governed Kartli and later received the crown of Kakheti, administered locally by his son David. His career connects Bagrationi exile with service to the shah.
Impulsó la codificación jurídica, la imp: He promoted legal codification, printing and Georgian written culture. His career was shaped by Persian investiture, Ottoman pressure and Russian assistance that failed to secure his power; he ended his life in exile in Russia.
Su carrera en la administración safávida: His career in the safe administration preceded a long reign in Kartli. He combined fidelity to the sah, agreements with local nobles and protection of Christian institutions. After defeating Teimuraz, he extended his authority to Kakheti and prepared a succession for adoption.
Hijo de Bagrat VII, heredó un poder estr: Son of Bagat VII, inherited a power closely dependent on Persia. The Georgian rebellion of 1625 moved his authority and favored Teimuraz I. His death closed another saving attempt to stabilise Kartli through this dynastic branch.
Recibió la corona kajetia en el contexto: He received the kajetia crown in the context of the safapvid collapse and briefly occupied Tiflis in front of Vajtang VI. The Ottoman intervention altered his alliances and ended his death. His brother Teimuraz then reorganized the eastern power.
Hija de Amadeo VII y Bona de Berry, se c: Daughter of Amadeus VII and Bona de Berry, she married Juan James of Montferrat. She was the mother of William VIII, Bonifacio III and Isabel, wife of Ludovico I of Saluzzo. Her position links several neighboring houses by filiation, but the alliances and conflicts of her descendants show that sharing ancestors did not guarantee political cooperation.
Hijo de Teodoro II, heredó Monferrato y: A son of Theodore II, he inherited Montferrat and married Joanna of Savoy, sister of Amadeus VIII. Their kinship did not prevent the Savoyrd duke from exerting pressure on his lands.
Hija de Juan Jacobo de Monferrato y Juan: The daughter of John James of Montferrat and Joan of Savoy, he married Ludovico I of Saluzzo. His son Ludovico II thus gathered ancestry from the Saluzzo, the Italian Paleologists and the Savoy.
Hijo de Juan Jacobo y Juana de Saboya, c: The son of Juan Jacobo and Juana de Savoy, combined the government of Montferrat with the military service of the Italian powers. His daughters married Ludovico II of Saluzzo and Charles I of Savoy.
Hijo de Juan Jacobo, sucedió a su herman: Son of John Jacob, he succeeded his brother William VIII when expectations surrounding the Montferrat inheritance already affected Savoy and Saluzzo. His sons William IX and John George continued the male line of the Palaeologoi.
Combatió primero la intervención safávid: He first fought the safavid intervention and spent years in captivity in Persia. Freed to fight the Ottomans, he re-ruled before falling prisoner to them. His two stages of government were separated so as not to present captivity as effective power.
Tamar de Imericia, reina de Kartli: Tamar of Imereti, Queen of Kartli
Defendió la autonomía de Kartli frente a: He defended Kartli's autonomy from his Safer campaigns. He died as a result of his battle with Garisi and his son Simon continued his resistance. The sources differ about some years of his reign, here from 1527 to 1556.
Hija de Bagrat III de Imericia, su matri: The daughter of Agrat III of Imereti, his marriage with Luarsab I united the two western and eastern branches of the Bagratii. He was the mother of Simon I and David XI, and his challenges followed different policies with respect to saving power.
Hija de Levan de Kajetia y esposa de Sim: The daughter of Levan of Kakheti and wife of Simon I of Kartli. His family linked the two Eastern monarchies through their children and grandchildren; these marriages coexisted with political rivalries and with the intervention of Persia and the Ottomans.
Asumió el gobierno tras la captura de su: He assumed his government after his father Simon's capture by the Ottoman. He co-operated with Abbas I with them and tried to open up contacts with Russia. His offspring connect Kartli's succession with the court of Teimuraz I of Kakheti.
Dependió del respaldo de Mingrelia para: He depended on Mingrelia's backing to attain and regain the throne. His reign included a break during the intervention of Simon of Kartli and his Western rivals, so two mandates are recorded.
Accedió al trono siendo adolescente y tu: He came to the throne as a teenager and had to face family rebellions and intervention from the neighboring principalities. He was deposed and died captive, leaving open the struggle for control of the Western monarchy.
Buscó protección rusa sin romper por com: He sought Russian protection while maintaining ties with Persia. His son David briefly removed him from power; after regaining it, he died in another family coup led by Constantine. The two phases of his reign have separate entries.
Desplazó a su padre Alejandro II y ocupó: He moved his father Alexander II and occupied his throne for about a year. His death allowed Alexander's restoration. Through his wife Ketevan and his son Teimuraz his line was linked to resistance to Abbas I.
Criado en Persia, encabezó el golpe que: Reborn in Persia, his father Alexander II was killed and his government provoked a rebellion with Ketevan and his death before his power was built up. His case shows the limits of his Safful intervention in his succession.
Conocido como Daud Kan tras su conversió: Known as Daud Khan after converting to Islam, he was promoted by the Safavids against his brother Simon. His control depended on Persian support and ended with the Ottoman offensive. His son Rostom would govern Kartli decades later.
Criado en el ambiente de la corte persa,: Raised in the Persian court environment, he was installed by Abbas I after the fall of Luarsab II. His authority depended on the safavid presence and was limited outside the centers that he controlled.
Su reinado terminó bajo la presión de Ab: His reign ended under the pressure of Abbas I, who lured him to Persia and held him captive. He was executed after refusing to convert to Islam. The Georgian Church venerated him as a martyr, linking his memory to the religious defense of the kingdom.
Hijo de Felipe III de Francia, dio orige: The son of Philip III of France, he gave origin to the branch of Évreux. He married Margaret of Artois and was father to Philip, future king of Navarre for his marriage to Joan II. His position explains the kinship of the new house without confusing him with the filiation proper to the Navarren queen.
Consorte de la dinastía Artois. Su traye: Consort of the Artois dynasty. Their life was connected with France.
Felipe de Évreux (Felipe III de Navarra): Felipe de Évre (Felipe III de Navarra)
Fue rey de Navarra por su matrimonio con: He was king of Navarre for his marriage to Juana II. He participated in peninsular campaigns and died after the expedition against Algeciras.
Hija de Felipe de Évreux y Juana II de N: The daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she was the wife of Peter IV of Aragon. Her marriage linked the new ruling Navarren house to the Aragonese monarchy.
Reina consorte de Francia y de Navarra d: Queen consort of France and Navarra from his marriage with Charles IV at 1325 to his death at 1328 and crowned at 1326. He did not exercise his own government.
Hija de Luis de Évreux y Margarita de Ar: The daughter of Louis of Évre and Margaret of Artois, married Charles IV of France. Her marriage connected the branch of Évre with the main line of the Capet kings.
Reina consorte de Francia y Navarra: Queen consort of France and Navarre
Intervino activamente en las crisis de l: He was active in the French monarchy's crises during the Hundred Years' War. His Navarren and Norman domains allowed him to act on both sides of the Pyrenees.
Hija de Felipe de Évreux y Juana II de N: Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Philip VI of France. The marriage brought the Navarrese house into close connection with the first generation of Valois rulers.
Hija de Roger IV de Foix, se casó con Ja: Daughter of Roger IV of Foix, she married James II of Majorca. The union connected the Pyrenean house with a monarchy whose inheritance included both island and continental lands. Their descendants illustrate the Mediterranean reach of the Foix family.
Conde de Foix en el siglo XIII, precedió: Count of Foix in the 13th century, preceded the generation that had been intertwined with Bearne with his father Roger Bernardo III and his son, Rojo Bernardo III, and his marriage with his family and his family.
Recibió de Jaime I un conjunto de domini: He received from James I a set of domains separated from the inheritance of his brother Pedro III. The relationship of dependence and rivalry with Aragon conditioned the Mallorcan kingdom.
Consorte de la dinastía Barcelona. Su tr: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life was connected with Naples.
Consort of the Casa de Aragón dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile, Mallorca.
Infante de la dinastía Casa de Aragón. S: Infante de la dynasty Casa de Aragón. Their life is linked to Mallorca.
Gobernó un reino condicionado por la sup: He ruled a kingdom conditioned by the supremacy of Aragon and his possessions on both sides of the Pyrenees. The absence of children caused the succession to fall to his nephew Jaime III.
Su matrimonio con Margarita de Bearne vi: His marriage to Margarita de Bearne linked the county of Foix with the rights over the Viscounty of the Bearnes. The accumulation of both estates gave his descendants a weighty position on both sides of the Pyrenees.
Hijo de Roger Bernardo III y de Margarit: A son of Roger Bernard III and Margaret of Béarn, he continued the joint inheritance of Foix and Béarn. His sons founded different lines within the family: those of Gaston II and Roger Bernard of Castellbò.
Hijo de Gastón I de Foix, representa la: Son of Gaston I of Foix, represents the family branch established in the province of Castellbó. This line retained its own position with respect to the main one.
Hijo y sucesor de Raimundo Roger, fue co: He was the son and successor of Raimundo Roger and was Count of Foix from 1223 to 1241. His marriage with Ermesenda (1208) united the VisCountryships of Castellbó and Cerdaña to his house. His protection of the albgenes and his rejection of the Inquisition earned him new excomisons.
Perdió el reino frente a Pedro IV de Ara: He lost the kingdom to Pedro IV of Aragon. His attempt to recover it ended with his death in the battle of Llucmajor.
Consorte de la dinastía Sabran. Su traye: Consort of the Sabran dynasty. Their life is linked to Mallorca.

Duque de Baviera, 1666–1705 (rama). Duqu: Duke of Bavaria, 1666–1705 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.
Segismundo Francisco sucedió a su herman: Segismund Francisco succeeded his brother Fernando Carlos in 1662. His death without a male heir in 1665 closed the Tyrolean branch; the county passed to Leopold I.
Duque titular de Lorena, ocupada por Fra: The titular Duke of Lorraine, occupied by France, and Marshal in the service of Emperor Leopold I. He sent the imperial troops to the rescue of Vienna (1683) and the seizure of Buda (1686).

Consorte de la dinastía Piast. Su trayec: Consort of the Piast dynasty. Their life is linked to Poland.
Carlos Roberto de Anjou afirmó su autori: Charles Robert of Anjou asserted his authority against the great Hungarian magnates. His reorganisation of royal revenues and mining strengthened the monarchy.
Bosnia y Ragusa conservaron gobiernos pr: Bosnia and Ragusa retained their own governments under the superiority of Louis. Lazar and Rastislalić ties are territorially distinguished and cut before documented crises; the plot does not mean direct Hungarian administration.
Valaquia alternó pactos y guerra: no se: Wallachia alternated pacts and war: no uninterrupted vassallage is represented. The annual payment of 7,000 ducats agreed with Venice in Turin (1381) does not become political vassalage of the entire Republic. The campaigns and occupations of Naples neither accredit a permanent Neapolitan dependency.
Podolia reconoce a Luis por el homenaje: Podolia recognizes Louis for the tribute of the Koriatovich of September 1377. For Pedro I of Moldova, the Angevin dependence of the late 1370s is a documentary and numismatic interpretation: it is labeled as inferred and only three nuclei are pointed out, without turning it into a unanimous chronology.
La herencia de la corona polaca añadió u: The Polish crown inheritance added a personal union to his Hungarian monarchy. The succession of his daughters Mary and Eduviges later separated the trajectories of both kingdoms.
Reforzó la administración y la legislaci: He strengthened Polish administration and legislation and promoted the foundation of the University of Krakow. He was the last Polish king of the main line of the Piast.

Rey de Hungría y Bohemia y posteriorment: King of Hungary and Bohemia and later emperor. He participated in the politics of the Great Schism, the Hussite wars and the Council of Constance, becoming a central figure of the 15th century Europe.
Carlos III de Nápoles y II de Hungría: Charles III of Naples and II of Hungary
Nápoles comienza en 1381 por coronación: Naples begins in 1381 by coronation and conquest; 1382 is the death of Joan I. Corfu and Butrinto are consulted as Neapolitan domains since 1382. Achaia and Jerusalem are nominal titles. Ragusa preserved his institutions and opposed Charles: the dependence of the Hungarian Crown does not credit a personal tribute to this king. Charles is not transferred the vassals of Louis I without his own evidence.
Carlos de Durazzo gobernó Croacia y Dalm: Charles of Durazzo governed Croatia and Dalmatia on behalf of Louis I before taking the Neapolitan throne in 1381. His domains included Corfu and Butrint; his authority over Achaea was contested by the Navarrese Company. Crowned king of Hungary and Croatia on 31 December 1385, he was attacked in Buda in February 1386 and died shortly afterwards. His title to Jerusalem did not confer control of the Holy Land.
Su acceso al trono húngaro desencadenó u: Her accession to the Hungarian throne triggered a crisis involving her mother, the magnates and Charles of Durazzo. Her marriage to Sigismund of Luxembourg linked him to the crown.
La muerte violenta de Wenceslao III exti: The violent death of Wenceslas III extinguished the male line of the Přemysl ruling Bohemia. His claims about Poland and Hungary show the extent and fragility of that dynastic expansion.
Viuda de Carlos III, ejerció la regencia: A widow of Charles III, he exercised the regency of Naples by his son Ladislao. The dispute with the branch of Anjou forced to sustain power from reduced bases and to negotiate supports; his intervention preserved the rights of the house of Durazzo.
Duque de Baviera, 1290–1312 (rama). Duqu: Duke of Bavaria, 1290–1312 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.
Fue capturado en Agincourt y pasó muchos: He was captured in Agincourt and spent many years in prison in England. His poetic work made him a prominent figure in French court literature.

La enfermedad de Carlos VI lo convirtió: Charles VI’s illness made him one of the leading contenders for control of the French monarchy. His murder on the orders of John the Fearless intensified the war between Armagnacs and Burgundians.
Consorte de la dinastía Visconti. Su tra: Consort of the Visconti dynasty. Their life is linked to Milan, France.
Consorte de la dinastía Valois. Su traye: Consort of the Valois dynasty, their life is linked to France, England.
Consorte de la dinastía Armagnac. Su tra: Consort of the Armagnac dynasty. Their life was connected with France.
Consorte de la dinastía La Marck. Su tra: Consort of the La Marck dynasty. Their life was connected with France, Cleves.
Rey de Francia que intervino de forma de: King of France who intervened decisively in the wars of Italy. His reign combined dynastic ambition in Milan and Naples with reforms that consolidated his popularity in the kingdom.
Conde de Angulema, 1407–1467. Conde de l: Count of Angulture, 1407–1467. Count of the Valois-Orléans dynasty.
Conde de la dinastía Valois-Orleans. Su: Count of the Valois-Orléans dynasty. Their life was connected with France, Orléans.
Margarita de Orleans, condesa de Étampes: Margarita de Orleans, Countess of Etampes
Hija de Luis de Orleans y de Valentina V: The daughter of Louis of Orleans and Valentina Visconti, married Richard of Brittany. His son Francis II became a duchy and became father of Anne of Brittany. Through Margarita, that heiress Bretona was connected with families of Orleans and Milan before their own actual marriages.
Heredó los derechos sobre Bretaña y fue: She inherited the rights to Brittany and became queen consort through her marriage to Francis I. The transmission of her inheritance contributed to the duchy’s union with the French crown.
Consort of the Valois-Orléans dynasty. Their life was connected with France, Ferrara.
Rey de Francia cuyo prolongado reinado q: King of France whose long reign was shaped by severe health crises and the civil war between Armagnacs and Burgundians, during the English offensive in the Hundred Years’ War.
Rey de Francia que recuperó la mayor par: King of France who recovered most of the territory lost to England. Joan of Arc’s intervention, military reform and reconciliation with Burgundy were central to his recovery.
Rey de Francia que debilitó a los grande: King of France who weakened the great feudal principalities and strengthened royal authority. His rivalry with Charles the Bold proved decisive in the acquisition of much of the Burgundian inheritance.
Fue un gran mecenas y coleccionista en l: A major patron and collector in Valois France. The Très Riches Heures, commissioned from the Limbourg brothers, are the most celebrated example of his patronage.
Conocido como Arturo de Richemont, fue h: Known as Arthur of Richemont, he was the son of John IV of Brittany and Joan of Navarre. He had an important career as Constable of France before inheriting the duchy in 1457.
Último rey efectivo de la Armenia cilici: Last effective king of the cilitia Armenia, Sis lost to the Mamluks in 1375 and spent years in captivity. Liberated, he traveled through European courts seeking support. His stay in Castile and his death in Paris connect the end of the kingdom with Western Europe.
Sucedió a su tío Enrique II y afianzó un: He succeeded his uncle Henry II and established a new Lusignan branch. His marriage alliances brought the island closer to Bourbon and Aragon. He abdicated in favour of Peter I while retaining the titular dignity of Jerusalem.
Enrique II de Chipre y Jerusalén: Henry II of Cyprus and Jerusalem
Último rey de Jerusalén que gobernó desd: The last king of Jerusalem to rule from Acre. After the fall of the city in 1291 he retained the title of Jerusalem while continuing as king of Cyprus.
Juan de Lusignan, regente de Chipre: John of Lusignan, regent of Cyprus
Hermano de Pedro I, gobernó durante la m: Brother of Peter I, he ruled during the minority of Peter II. The accusations and revenges that followed the king's murder confronted the members of the court. His title as Prince of Antioch was nominal, as the principality had disappeared.

Príncipes de Transilvania cuyas alianzas: Princes of Transylvania whose family alliances extended to Croatia and Hungary.
Los Châtillon fueron una casa nobiliaria: The Châtillon were a French noble house with several branches, one of which inherited Blois County and was linked to the ducal succession of Brittany through Charles of Blois.

Martín V Colonna: una familia romana cie: Martin V Colonna: a Roman family closes the schism

Sixto IV: cardenales, señoríos y una gen: Sixtus IV: Cardinals, Lordships and a whole generation of nephews

León X y Clemente VII: dos papas dentro: Leo X and Clement VII: two popes from the same Medici family
León X es hijo de Lorenzo el Magnífico y: Leon X is the son of Lorenzo the Magnificent and Clarice Orsini. His cousin Giulio, the son of Giuliano de’ Medici, will arrive later as Clement VII. 1527: una familia poderosa no puede prot: 1527: a powerful family cannot protect Rome from Europe
Clemente VII intenta maniobrar entre Fra: Clement VII tries to maneuver between France and Charles V and ends up caught in a catastrophe: the Sack of Rome. Paulo III: del parentesco Borgia al duca: Paul III: from Borgia kinship to Parma duchy

Clemente VIII: el cardenal-nepote como o: Clement VIII: Cardinal-Nepote as Government Office
Con los Aldobrandini el nepotismo se vue: With the Aldobrandini, nepotism becomes increasingly institutional. Pietro Aldobrandini, nephew of the pope, accumulates missions, rents and diplomatic responsibilities. Cardinal-nepote occupies a recognizable position within the Roman court.
Paulo V y Scipione: poder, riqueza y una: Paul V and Scipione: power, wealth and a collection that will survive the pontificate

Alejandro VII: los Chigi llegan a Roma: Alexander VII: Chigi arrive in Rome

Inocencio XII: el sistema intenta cerrar: Innocent XII: the system tries to close itself
La constitución Romanum decet Pontificem: The Romanum Decet Pontificem Constitution formally restricts papal nepotism and limits the old model of the cardinal-nepot. Catalina de Médici, los hugonotes y la L: Catherine of Medici, Huguenots and the Catholic League
Francia pasa de una sucesión aparentemen: France goes from a seemingly secure succession to four decades of religious civil wars. Una muerte cambia el equilibrio de Franc: A Death Changes the Balance of France
Enrique II muere después de un accidente: Henry II dies after an accident in a tournament. His son Francis II is young, married to Maria Estuardo and politically dependent on the Guise, uncles of the queen. Catherine de Medici moves from the king’s wife to the mother of a vulnerable dynasty.
Catalina intenta gobernar entre dos part: Catherine tries to rule between two parties
Francisco II muere sin hijos y su herman: Francis II dies without children and his brother Charles IX ascends to the throne as a child. Wassy convierte la tensión en guerra civ: Wassy Turns Tension into Civil War

Catalina casa a su hija Margarita con En: Catherine houses her daughter Margarita with Enrique de Navarra, one of the great Huguenot princes, to strengthen peace. Enrique III vuelve de Polonia a una Fran: Henry III returns from Poland to a broken France
Carlos IX muere y su hermano Enrique aba: Charles IX dies and his brother Henry leaves the Polish crown to become Henry III of France. The Valois dynasty retains the throne, but the new king has no children and his brother Francis of Anjou is the last male heir of the family.
La muerte de un príncipe convierte la re: The death of a prince turns religion into succession

El rey mata al hombre que dominaba París: King kills man who dominated Paris

El último Valois entrega la sucesión a u: The last Valois hands over the succession to a Bourbon

Para ganar Francia, Enrique cambia de co: To win France, Henry changes confession

The reconstruction of the authority of the crown combines negotiation with both parties and the recognition of religious commitments.

Leopoldo I gobierna la frontera más peli: Leopold I rules the most dangerous border of the Empire
